opex.name: Research & development
opex.note: Designing the next chips and software — a smaller share of each revenue dollar than most chip rivals spend.

opex.name: Selling, general & administrative
opex.note: Selling the products and running the company.

opex.name: Amortization & restructuring
opex.note: Writing down the value of brands and technology bought in acquisitions (VMware above all) — a bookkeeping charge, not cash — plus restructuring costs.

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP)
kpis.note: vs $(0.31) a year ago from continuing operations

oneTimers: A $163M gain on the sale of a business sits inside other income, partly offsetting the quarter's $807M of interest expense.

The year-ago quarter (Q3 FY24) showed a net loss only because of a one-time $4,238M tax provision tied to moving intellectual property between subsidiaries; this quarter's tax was a normal $1,145M expense.
otherDetail: Interest expense of $807M on Broadcom's debt, partly offset by $205M of other income, net — which includes a $163M gain on the sale of a business — a net -$602M below operating profit.

segments.name: Semiconductor solutions
segments.note: Chips — above all custom AI accelerators and networking gear for data centers. AI semiconductor revenue grew 63% YoY to $5.2B, and Broadcom guided it to $6.2B in the next quarter.

segments.name: Infrastructure software
segments.note: VMware and other enterprise software — the steady, subscription side of the company, up 17% YoY.

takeaways.text: AI semiconductor revenue grew 63% YoY to $5.2B — custom accelerators and networking — and Broadcom guided it higher again, to $6.2B in Q4, an eleventh straight quarter of AI growth.
takeaways.title: AI revenue accelerated

takeaways.text: Free cash flow was a record $7,024M — 44% of revenue — because capital spending was only $142M. Broadcom returned $2.8B to shareholders in the quarter through cash dividends.
takeaways.title: Record free cash flow

takeaways.text: GAAP profit carries $2,026M of amortization of acquisition-related intangibles plus $213M of restructuring — mostly VMware bookkeeping, not cash. On Broadcom's non-GAAP view, net income was $8,404M instead of $4,140M.
takeaways.title: Non-GAAP profit was double

verdict: Broadcom's revenue grew 22% to a record $16.0B as AI revenue jumped 63% to $5.2B, and it kept $4.1B as profit — a year after a one-time tax charge had pushed the same quarter into the red.
